changelog: - **One tenant's spent broadcast band no longer stops other tenants' newsletters, and a held issue is no longer silent** (#2335). `dispatchDueNewsletters` runs on `runNewsletterTick` (`src/lib/newsletterQuotaHold.ts`, unit-tested). An issue the quota refuses no longer uses up one of the tick's 10 slots; every issue is still metered on its own; a tenant gets at most 10 held attempts per tick (only its further SCHEDULED issues are `deferred`); and a SENDING resume is never skipped. Before this, ten held issues from one tenant filled every tick. A held attempt no longer loads the issue's image. `queueScheduledNewsletter` now scopes its pending / last-sent / used-template reads to the default org it queues for, so another tenant's held issue cannot stop the cadence. A due issue that is held shows an "On hold" line in the `/admin/newsletters` history (`quotaHold` in `GET /api/admin/newsletters`, only for the viewing admin's own tenant) with the figures and reset date. The first cron refusal per issue per month writes a `newsletter.quota_hold` ActivityLog entry (`{ orgId, month }` only), and each tick that finds newly held issues sends one `ops-alert` mail to `ALERT_EMAIL_TO` naming them and their org. The all-or-nothing rule and the immutability of a sent issue are unchanged.

en: A newsletter issue held back by this month's broadcast quota now says so in the newsletter history, with the numbers and the date the meter resets, and still goes out by itself once the quota allows.
tr: Bu ayın yayın kotası yüzünden bekleyen bir bülten sayısı artık bülten geçmişinde bunu rakamlarla ve sayacın sıfırlanacağı tarihle gösteriyor; kota izin verdiğinde yine kendiliğinden gönderiliyor.
de: Eine Newsletter-Ausgabe, die wegen des monatlichen Versandkontingents zurückgehalten wird, zeigt das jetzt im Newsletter-Verlauf an – mit den Zahlen und dem Datum, an dem der Zähler zurückgesetzt wird. Sobald das Kontingent es erlaubt, wird sie weiterhin automatisch versendet.
